# Echo Agent

> Official discovery index for echo-agent and EKO. Chinese routes are the default; English routes use `/en`.

# echo-agent
Build agents from explicit, composable runtime parts.
A Rust workspace for ReAct execution, tools, context, tasks, subagents, integrations, and observable event streams. Product policy stays in the application that embeds it.
## Easy to start, powerful to compose
Runnable examples, focused crates, typed events, optional features, tests, and bilingual documentation keep the path from first run to extension explicit.
- Start: Runnable examples. Clone the repository, configure a provider, and run a checked-in example.
- Compose: Focused crates + features. ReAct, tools, skills, state, tasks, Subagents, and integrations stay at explicit boundaries.
- Learn: Typed APIs + bilingual docs. Typed events, examples, tests, guides, and references shorten change feedback.
## Framework capabilities
Every item below corresponds to code and documentation in the echo-agent workspace.
- Simple to start: Use the public builder and runnable examples to assemble and run a first agent.
- Powerful by composition: Combine ReAct, typed tools, skills, memory, tasks, Subagents, and streamed events.
- Fast feedback for iteration: Focused crates, feature flags, typed events, examples, and tests keep changes bounded.
- Bilingual documentation: Follow English and Chinese onboarding, concepts, references, and knowledge guides.
- Tasks and Subagents: Model task graphs and delegate bounded work through one Subagent vocabulary.
- Open integration boundaries: Connect MCP, LSP, channels, hooks, and tracing through optional adapters.

# EKO
One capable agent, built for your own machine.
EKO is the desktop, terminal, CLI, and channel application built on echo-agent. Its interfaces use the shared application core; capability parity across those interfaces is the product contract.
## Purpose-built local workspaces
Coding, data analysis, academic research, biomedical literature research, and long-horizon work are routed through explicit application profiles and inspectable local artifacts.
- Work profiles: Code · data · research. Each profile binds relevant tools and evidence expectations through the application core.
- Research trail: Sources + artifacts. Research connectors and workspaces keep sources, entities, citations, and outputs visible.
- Long horizon: Budget + checkpoint + resume. Task runtime state supports scheduled, pausable, and resumable work on the local machine.
## Work EKO is designed to carry
Each capability below is grounded in a production binding in the current application code. Duration and results depend on configuration, models, tools, and source availability.
- Coding: Work with files, shells, Git, LSP, isolated worktrees, and bounded Subagent runs.
- Data processing and analysis: Use data workspaces and Polars-backed tools with reviewable Python or R scripts, manifests, and artifacts.
- Academic research: Search arXiv and Semantic Scholar, work with Zotero, and retain sources in a research workspace.
- Biomedical literature research: Search PubMed and Europe PMC and organize biomedical entities and sources for literature synthesis, not diagnosis.
- Tens-of-hours long-horizon tasks: TaskRuntime, checkpoints, pause and resume, budgets, and scheduling support work designed to continue for hours or tens of hours.
- Complete local multi-interface agent: TUI, GUI, CLI, and channels use the shared application core; capability parity is the product contract.
